newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Gucci up to head ADR trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Gucci up to head ADR trade.

text.p: Luxury retailer Gucci Group N.V. rose on Tuesday to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Markets largely marked time while waiting for testimony from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan before a Senate committee.
Gucci rose 1-1/2 to 73-3/8, continuing a steady rise so far this month. The shares have risen from about 62 at the end of 1996, boosted by better-than-expected Christmas sales.
"It's been a very good performer. The high-end retailer seems to have a very strong resistance to generally lower retail sales," a trader said.
"People are buying brand names, that's for sure."

Among other European shares, British mobile phone operator Vodafone Group Plc rose 1-5/8 to 43-1/2. The company reported it had entered a deal with New York's Omnipoint Corp for Vodafone subscribers to use Omnipoint's network in the United States.

Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras was up 1/2 to a record 86-3/8 in moderate trade. The stock was boosted by prospects for opening up the Brazilian telephone market and a Morgan Stanley upgrade of the company's 12-month price target.
Analyst Luiz Carvalho raised his price target to $115 from $100, and told Reuters, "During the last few weeks and months we have seen a lot of regulatory progress in Brazil."
Decliners led advancers by 270 to 201 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 27.2 million shares.
